purpose: Verify the Stage-9.5 causal RESET-NACK and Stage-9.3 tagged recovery codecs across independent sender and receiver processes through a fault-injecting network proxy.
causal_rules: sender and receiver run as distinct operating-system processes
all protocol frames cross a network-proxy boundary as packed binary payloads
a dropped frame causes no destination state transition
a delayed frame is decoded only when the proxy later delivers its original bytes
the sender learns receiver boot and catalog state only from a delivered 32-bit RESET-NACK
activation or full installation restores codebook context only; a later compact update is required before action execution
receiver process restart clears volatile action state
durable catalog corruption must fail closed
no receiver function return value is converted into sender knowledge unless represented by a delivered frame
claim_boundary: This is desktop software protocol conformance evidence, not a hardware-in-the-loop or UAV deployment result.
The proxy injects registered logical faults and does not emulate RF propagation, operating-system timing, energy use, or real network-driver queues.
The 16-bit recovery tag detects accidental stale sessions and is not an authentication code.
A positive result does not reverse the failed Stage-6 external Final and does not prove clean-bit superiority on external spectrum data.
